Thanks again for taking the call today, Mark — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Call recap:
- Target flighting use case: personalized product recommendations in the cart flow (low-latency, streaming-friendly).
- Traffic shape: steady stream during peaks (10k qps across service, ~300 concurrent inference requests per region), average request size ~600 tokens (prompt + context), some longer sessions up to 2k tokens.
- Desired SLOs: p95 latency <= 150ms for streaming responses (user-visible completions), p99 <= 350ms for batch/ranking endpoints.
- Availability: regional failover between us-west and us-east; preference for dedicated pools if possible for predictability.

Primary asks from today:
1) We’ll provide representative payloads (sample prompts, avg/95/99 token lengths) and 24h traffic histogram.
2) Redwood to provide options for meeting the latency SLO with estimated cost and recommended levers (batching, caching, quantization, model variants).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi to validate perf assumptions and run a small lab test (repro with your payloads).

Cost & perf levers (high level):
- Continuous batching: reduces per-token compute by grouping small requests; helps when concurrency is moderate (we’ll show expected latency vs cost curve).
- KV/prefix caching: beneficial for repeated user prefixes or product-context tokens; can cut token compute significantly for repeated patterns.
- Quantization profiles: 8-bit/4-bit quantization options with measured throughput gains; tradeoff is small accuracy delta — Rishi can show eval numbers.
- Model variants: serving a smaller quantized model for low-latency ranking and routing to a larger model for high-quality long-form generation.

Next steps (action items):
- Mark: share sample payloads and a 24h histogram by end of day Monday.
- Redwood: attach SLO template and a short options PDF (attached).
- Rishi & Neha: coordinate a 1-hour technical deep-dive next week; proposed times sent in follow-up.

I attached an SLO template and a short doc summarizing the perf levers (see attachments). If anything here is off, flag it and I’ll adjust.

Hi Mark — Rishi here (Solutions/Inference). Quick answers + what we can validate in the deep-dive/lab run:

1) p95 measurement:
- We typically measure p95 as end-to-end server-side latency for request completion. For streaming use cases we also provide per-chunk latency metrics; UX teams commonly target per-chunk p95 < 100–150ms to keep perceived latency low. We’ll include both in the template.

2) Quantization impact on quality:
- In our benchmarks on recommendation-style prompts (~200–800 tokens), 8-bit quantization is essentially lossless for ranking tasks; 4-bit can show small regressions in edge cases (0.5–2% drop in top-1 retrieval/IOU metrics depending on prompt diversity).
- We always recommend evaluation against a small held-out prompt set from your traffic. We can run an A/B with your payloads.

3) Streaming + KV/prefix caching:
- KV caching works at the model KV-cache level (prefix tokens). For streaming, if the cache contains common prefixes, servers can seed the KV cache and begin streaming without recomputing the prefix. In practice, streaming + cache is supported; you get the latency benefits for repeated prefixes. For truly per-request unique contexts, caching has limited benefit.

4) Continuous batching & concurrency:
- Continuous batching is effective when you have many small requests; it groups them with tight latency-aware windows. For your 300 concurrent requests, we expect up to 20–40% reduction in per-token GPU time while holding p95 within target if windows are tuned. We’ll show latency vs batching window tradeoffs.

5) Model variants & routing:
- Typical pattern: small quantized model (low-latency) for ranking and short completions; route to larger/fluid models for longer generative flows. We support automated routing policies (latency-first vs quality-first) with automatic fallbacks.

What we propose for the lab run:
- You provide 24h histogram and representative payloads + target traffic profile (concurrency & qps).
- We run a 4–8 hour microbenchmark in our lab: compare baseline (fp16) vs 8-bit vs 4-bit; with and without continuous batching; with/without KV caching; measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
- Deliverable: a short report with recommended config (batching window, cache TTLs, quantization profile, model variant) and cost/latency curves.

If this plan looks good I’ll book a 1-hour slot and bring the perf harness. Suggested slots: Tue/Wed 10–12 or Thu 2–4 PT.

Thanks — Rishi
